candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Health Promotion and Maintenance, printed p.9 / PDF p.13
candidate.educational_objective: Teach parents why asymptomatic children with lead-exposure risk may still require testing.

options.A: Children may have no obvious symptoms; no safe blood lead level has been identified, and at-risk children should be tested.
options.B: Lead exposure is harmless unless the child has seizures.
options.C: A child without symptoms cannot have lead in the blood.
options.D: Lead-based paint is found only in homes built after 1978.

candidate.rationale: CDC states that no safe blood lead level in children has been identified and that even low levels can affect development and learning. Many exposed children have no obvious symptoms. Homes built before 1978 are an important potential source, and children at risk should receive blood lead testing.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Lead exposure may be asymptomatic; no safe blood lead level is known, and at-risk children should be tested.
candidate.source_document_title: Testing for Lead Poisoning in Children; Preventing Childhood Lead Poisoning
candidate.source_locator: Testing—children may have no symptoms and at-risk children should be tested; prevention—pre-1978 housing and no safe blood lead level
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
candidate.stem: Parents of a 3-year-old living in a home built before 1978 say the child seems healthy, so they do not think lead exposure matters. Which teaching is most accurate?
